title: Review + delivery / evidence and authority
subtitle: Review, commit and branch disposition retain separate authority; release preparation stops at its PR.

nodes.title: /review · /checkpoint
nodes.body:
/review: current diff
/checkpoint: periodic codebase sweep
/preview predicts only; no verdict
/tribunal and /threat-model are opt-in

nodes.title: Fresh inputs → scoped reviewer fleet
nodes.body:
Select current context for each reviewer
Required refs + native instruction order
Deliver to that actual child, not its parent
Then dispatch by the actual diff paths
Preserve capability and evidence gaps

nodes.title: finding-triage
nodes.body:
Collect and deduplicate findings
Retain terminal states / gaps
Classify severity and scope
Then pass the complete report onward

nodes.title: verdict-aggregator
nodes.body:
Read-only in-memory result
Own change: CRITICAL/HIGH blocks PR
Inbound PR: local verdict; post separately
Checkpoint: explicit dated persistence

nodes.title: /commit
nodes.body:
Current staged scope
TDD complete where applicable
Typed plans: current acceptance
No status-label substitutes

nodes.title: Phases 1–3 / authorize + scope
nodes.body:
1 Explicit permission
2 Non-protected branch
3 Homogeneous change classification
No implied authorization from approval
of a specification or an implementation

nodes.title: Phases 4–6 / prove + inspect
nodes.body:
4 Focused tests, lint, secrets, scope gates
5 Fresh behavioral proof
5.5 Legacy v1 staged-source auto-heal
6 Complete diff review
v2 pairs require native selected updates

nodes.title: Phases 7–9 / persist
nodes.body:
7 Harvest → explicitly selected paths
8 Conventional Commit message
9 Commit → SHA + clean-tree report
No blanket staging; failed hook returns
to correction, not gate circumvention

nodes.title: Conditional scope gates / they do not add new public routes
nodes.body: crypto-compliance + secret-handling → auth-crypto-reviewer; migrations → migration-reviewer; CI/deploy → security-reviewer; dependencies → dependency-reviewer.

nodes.title: /pr
nodes.body:
Direct open request or
feature/sprint terminal handoff
Choose mode from user authority

nodes.title: --watch / retained /watch
nodes.body:
Detached hosted-CI watcher
Red → diagnosis; green → offer, never auto-merge

nodes.title: --cleanup / retained /cleanup
nodes.body:
post-merge-cleanup
Prove fetched containment, classify residue
Confirm each discard; preserve unique work

nodes.title: Creation / current-head preflight
nodes.body:
Current acceptance + commit proof
Branch / base / head / diff
Applicable ADR ancestry
Missing or stale proof → owner repair

nodes.title: Open-PR procedure in this owner
nodes.body:
Applicable reviewers; clear blockers
Compose summary, test plan and ADR links
Push branch, create PR, return URL
Never re-invoke the PR wrapper

nodes.title: Merge via PR / only if selected
nodes.body:
Explicit user authority + exact-head CI
Revalidate ancestry and bound head

nodes.title: Open PR / authorized disposition
nodes.body:
Sprint ends at open PR
Feature keeps selected terminal option
Discard requires stated-loss confirmation

nodes.title: /release · selected target
nodes.body:
Resolve declared target + policy
Prepare reviewed release surfaces
Dry-run stops at its report

nodes.title: Release preparation PR
nodes.body:
Commit through normal gates
Name assets + declared publisher
Open release PR and STOP

nodes.title: Qualified hosted continuation
nodes.body:
Only after the release PR merges
Exact fetched head + green evidence
Compose the bound tag and cohort

nodes.title: Publication and closeout
nodes.body:
Consume applicable cohort authority
Read back release + inventory
Declared receipt closes by separate PR

nodes.title: Selected legacy resolution
nodes.body:
Actual merge + schema-1 provenance
Exact current HEAD chosen
Native or uncertain ownership refuses

nodes.title: Inspect → exact binding
nodes.body:
Shipped helper inspects Git + files
Pass the returned binding directly
Changed identities refuse

nodes.title: Restore HEAD only
nodes.body:
One supported conflict rendering
Exact committed code-map bytes
Provenance and index untouched

nodes.title: Review, stage, re-prove
nodes.body:
Inspect the resulting diff
Use normal explicit staging
Review + CI bind the integrated head

panels.title: 01  /  REVIEW IS A SCOPED, READ-ONLY EVIDENCE PATH
panels.caption: Select by actual scope. Routine reports, change blockers and independent typed-authority reviews have different contracts.

panels.title: 02  /  /commit → commit-gate
panels.caption: A local commit is the output. Every later action must retain its own requested scope and authority.

panels.title: 03  /  /pr → SELECT THE MODE BEFORE CREATION PREFLIGHT
panels.caption: Watch and cleanup are early return paths, not steps that must first create a PR.

panels.title: 04  /  CONDITIONAL LEGACY CODE-MAP RECOVERY
panels.caption: Only inside an authorized integration, after the exact-HEAD resolution is already selected. No extra approval is invented.

panels.title: 05  /  /release → DECLARED TARGETS + SEPARATE PUBLICATION AUTHORITY
panels.caption: A release is not an automatic continuation of a green PR. A release commit still goes through commit-gate.

notes.text: SDD combined-scope review has its own caller rules. Claude authority-reviewer serves frozen typed targets; no generic reviewer result fabricates its receipt.
Actual reviewer delivery is bound to actor/task/worktree/epochs. A source-current identity, parent marker or author packet is not reviewer proof.
Local checks are impact-bounded; exhaustive repository and platform proof is exact-head hosted CI before merge. A previously green head is not current evidence.
Content/path-bound security-pass behavior is retained from the baseline. New context and debug contracts do not waive existing specialist gates.
Informational reports return to their caller. Nothing in the review path grants authority to edit, commit, file issues, merge, publish or spend.
